headline: Inworld, a voice AI company, has bought Ultravox, the platform developers use to build voice agents that talk with people in real time.
score_reason: Lowered from 4 to 3: the deal was announced on 30 Sep 2026, before the edition window, and the company gave no price or numbers.
importance_line: It affects developers and businesses that run voice agents on Ultravox, who keep working as before and get upgraded voices, and the two companies, but the announcement is the buyer's own and gives no price or deal terms.
summary: Inworld says in a company blog post dated 30 Sep 2026 that it has bought Ultravox, a platform developers use to build voice agents, with the Ultravox team members who joined it continuing to develop the product. Existing customers need no changes and Inworld voices on Ultravox now run on a newer text-to-speech model at no extra cost, but the post gives no price or other deal terms.
notes: Original outlet GeekWire (https://www.geekwire.com/2026/seattle-voice-ai-startup-ultravox-formerly-known-as-fixie-acquired-by-inworld/) was blocked, as were Business Wire and Dealroom; wrote from Inworld's own blog post, so source and url are Inworld's. This is the buyer's own announcement. The Seattle and formerly Fixie details appear only in the GeekWire headline, so they are left out.
